Setup downloads about 523 MB of models once per machine, needs network access to Hugging Face and needs a writable model cache. `--skip-models` postpones the download until indexing, while search still requires the models. sweet-search is a local code-navigation package with six `ss-*` commands: hybrid search, exact grep, semantically ranked pattern search, semantic spans within one file, symbol tracing and exact file reads. Its `sweet-search` CLI also handles setup, indexing, daemon control, status, updates and uninstall. The optional stdio MCP server registers eight tools: `search`, `trace`, `index`, `health`, `repo-map`, `vocab-prewarm`, `read` and `read-semantic`. The index combines AST-aware chunks and code-graph context with six retrieval structures: word search, sparse n-grams, binary HNSW, dense vectors, late-interaction vectors and a code graph. The default index path rebuilds the graph and updates vectors for changed files. A watcher then applies edits incrementally and publishes index changes atomically. The README says saved edits are usually searchable within seconds, with a documented budget of at most 50 files and 10 CPU seconds per update. The README says code never leaves the machine, but that statement is not unconditional in the implementation. During graph-summary generation, the provider selector prefers Groq or Cerebras when their API keys are configured, and the summary prompt can include up to 2,000 characters of source code. In the opencode report, native ran subagents in 109 rollouts: the modeled reduction falls to 4.3% without those runs, despite the reported 34.4% aggregate. **A new mcp-tooling mode has a larger routing cost than this local search service appears to earn.** The hub currently owns eight modes through a two-stage router, mode registry and packet-local resource map. Adding a member requires aligned registry and router entries, a packet and regenerated leaf metadata, then routing replay. The shared Code Mode substrate is already outside the hub.
